prompt: In the famous marshmallow experiments, young children could eat one treat now or wait and receive two. What did the waiting strategy of looking away or covering the treat demonstrate?

options.text: That willpower is fixed at birth and cannot be helped
That managing attention — not just resisting harder — helps delay gratification
That the children who waited did not like marshmallows
That rewards should never be delayed

explanation: Children who waited successfully tended to manage their attention — looking away, covering the treat, or inventing distractions — rather than staring at the reward and relying on raw resistance. The same trick powers waiting lists and out-of-sight savings.
